chapter_title: [Concerning the Interpretation of] all [the] Fathers of [Light], who are distinguished from one another.
chapter_note: This chapter preserves a systematic correspondence catalog mapping cosmic functions to divine beings. The substrate is dominant: ¶2-11 are pure oldest-layer teaching in the consistent 'The beginning of X is Y' pattern. Both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system — function (grace, counsel, building, delivering, wisdom) mapped to cosmic being. The opening is wrapped in dialogue frame + devotional address, and the closing has two beatitude paragraphs. Gardner's note about catechetical instruction is apt — this reads like a systematized reference list. Negative editorial fatigue (-1.08) confirms the substrate holds through the chapter with minimal drift.

paragraphs.core_text: The beginning of every good grace is the great Father of the [ligh]ts; since [a]ll [graces] are given by his hand.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Once again the enlightener speaks:' (dialogue frame formula) and 'Happen you know, my beloved ones, that' (devotional address to audience). The remaining teaching follows the catalog pattern identical to ¶2-11.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The dialogue frame attribution and 'my beloved ones' address are compiler additions. The core teaching — 'The beginning of X is Y' — is the first entry in the systematic catalog.

paragraphs.core_text: The beginning of each blessing and every prayer is the Mother of [L]ife, the first Holy Spirit.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second catalog entry. Maps blessing/prayer → Mother of Life. 'The first Holy Spirit' is standard Manichaean cosmological nomenclature for this entity, not a Christian overlay. Institutional score (11.76) triggered by 'prayer' but prayer here is a cosmic function, not an institutional practice. Both sides stay within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, [the] beginning [of] every good [co]unsel is the T[h/i]rd Am[bassad]or, the king of the glorious realm that lies in this [wo]rld, [ ... ] of the King of the lights.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third catalog entry. Maps counsel → Third Ambassador. The additional phrase 'the king of the glorious realm that lies in this world' is a cosmic-geographical descriptor, not editorial application. Lacuna obscures what may have been a further qualifier relating him to the King of the lights.

paragraphs.core_text: The beginning of [ ... and] each [hono]ur (?) is the Beloved of the Lights, who is honour[ed.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fourth entry. Maps honour → Beloved of the Lights. Lacuna and uncertain reading ('?') suggest manuscript damage. The epithet 'Beloved of the Lights' is cosmic nomenclature.

paragraphs.core_text: The beginning of a]ll [the trappers] and hunters is the First [Man.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fifth entry. Maps trapping/hunting → First Man. 'Trappers and hunters' as cosmic function corresponds to the First Man's role in engaging Darkness — a cosmic combat function rendered through correspondential imagery.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.44⟩
... of] all fighters is [the] Living [Spirit], the Father of Life, who has distribu[ted about] his five sons from place to place.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Sixth entry. Maps fighting → Living Spirit. 'Who has distributed about his five sons from place to place' describes cosmic architecture — the five sons stationed across the cosmos. This functional elaboration follows the same pattern as other entries (cf. ¶11). Opening lost to lacuna but clearly part of the catalog.

paragraphs.core_text: The beginning of all the archit[e]cts and builders is the Great Builder, who is glorious.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Seventh entry. Maps building/architecture → Great Builder. Cosmic function rendered through craft correspondence. Clean substrate with no overlay.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, the first of all the porters of the gr[e]a[t]ness is the Pillar of Glory ... [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Eighth entry. Maps porter function (bearing/carrying) → Pillar of Glory. Note variant formula: 'the first of' rather than 'the beginning of' — but same structural function. Lacuna at end may have contained further description.

paragraphs.core_text: The beginning of [all] the deliverers [is Jesus the Splendour]; or the one who delivers, as he frees whoever belongs [ ... ] from his words.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Ninth entry. Maps deliverance → Jesus the Splendour. The restoration '[is Jesus the Splendour]' is editorial conjecture but fits the catalog structure. 'Or the one who delivers' may be a translation gloss or alternative epithet. 'From his words' is unclear due to lacuna — possibly 'by his words' or the lacuna alters sense. Jesus the Splendour is a cosmic entity in the Manichaean system, not the historical Jesus.

paragraphs.core_text: The beginning of every wisdom of truth is the Virgin of Light, [.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Tenth entry. Maps wisdom → Virgin of Light. Broken off by manuscript damage. Both sides fully cosmic.

paragraphs.core_text: The beginning of] all [the great]est honoured ones [ ... ] is the Light Mind; who is the awakene[r of they] who sleep, the gatherer in of the ones who are sc[att]ered.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Eleventh and final catalog entry. Maps highest honour → Light Mind. The functional elaboration ('awakener of they who sleep, gatherer in of the ones who are scattered') describes cosmic operations — awakening trapped light-souls and gathering scattered light. Both sides within the cosmic system. This closes the systematic catalog.

Beatitude formula ('Blessed is he who') marks exhortation closure appended after the complete catalog. The seam flag correctly identifies this. 'Lodge this treasure within him' and 'fasten the knowledge of these fathers in his heart' are devotional injunctions. The clause 'they are the root of all the lights, and such as belong to all life' contains cosmological summary content subordinated to the exhortation — the editor is USING cosmic language to justify the beatitude, not teaching independently. Considered classifying as mixed but the cosmological content is too general and embedded within the exhortation structure to extract independently.

Second beatitude closure. 'Continue in their belief' and 'inherit with them eternal life for ever' are classic exhortation markers. 'For ever' is the devotional sealing formula. The seam flag correctly identifies this as editorial closure extending the teaching sequence.
